The US Navy was founded 250 years ago on October 13, 1775. Congratulations to the Navy and those who served in the Navy defending our nation.

My great uncle Fred William Schweinberg served in the Pacific on the USS Pennsylvania for several years until he transferred to the East Coast where he was the coxswain on the USS Mayflower, the Presidential Yacht. He later died in 1929 in Panama in an accident. He is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.

My father William F. Wertz was a 1st Class Radioman on the USS Hornet aircraft carrier in World WII serving under Admiral Jocko Clark. The ship was active in the Pacific theater, receiving a total of 9 battle stars, 7 of which were earned as the sole receiver in 1944 and 2 of which were earned as Hornet and air group together in 1945. She was one of 9 aircraft carriers to receive the Presidential Unit Citation.

During the war, the Hornet shot down 668 planes, destroyed another 742 on the ground, sank one cruiser, one carrier, 10 destroyers, 424 cargo ships and assisted in sinking the battleship Yamato. She had struck the first blow for the liberation of the Philippines; she was the first to hit Tokyo in a full-scale attack and she was the first to hit the Yamato. She spent a total of 52 days under Japanese air attack without being hit even by a machine gun bullet.

My aunt, Elizabeth Kofel was a member of the WAVES during World WII.  The WAVES stands for Women Accepted for Volunteer Emergency Service, the women's branch of the U.S. Naval Reserve established during World War II.
